name: pg_create_type_create_shell_type
subject: Don't create a shell type for function returning an array
goal:
CREATE FUNCTION may create a shell type automatically when a bare, unqualified argument or result type name does not yet exist. More complex type syntax is being treated as though it named such a type, leaving unwanted shell types behind after a failing command.

Exercise nonexistent return types written as an array, with a typmod, through `%TYPE` for a nonexistent column, and in a nonexistent schema. Each command must fail without creating a shell type. A bare eligible name must retain its existing shell-type behavior. Once a real type exists, normal validation of arrays and typmods must remain unchanged.
